matters.text:
Agenda Item Details 

 Meeting 
 Jun 11, 2026 - Blueprint Intergovernmental Meeting 
 Category 
 V. General Business- Presentations 
 Subject 
 7. Consideration of a Competitive Economic Development Project Proposal for Project Prestige 
 Type 

 STATEMENT OF ISSUE: 

 This item requests Blueprint Intergovernmental Agency Board (IA Board) approval of a competitive incentive package to support the expansion of a local manufacturing company, code named Project Prestige. Project Prestige represents a Tallahassee-Leon County-based advanced manufacturing company considering expansion within Innovation Park. The company's proposed expansion represents a $25 million capital investment, 100 new manufacturing and research jobs over the next 2 years, and a new 50,000 sq. ft. manufacturing center. The company did not submit its written request for confidentiality prior to the public meeting of the Competitive Projects Cabinet held on May 21, 2026. The name of the company was therefore disclosed at the public meeting and can be discussed pursuant to the requirements of section 288.075(2), Florida Statutes. Florida law, however, does provide that proprietary confidential business information held by an economic development agency is confidential and exempt from public disclosure under certain circumstances. This project is highly competitive as the company is also considering other locations for the new manufacturing facility. 
 FISCAL IMPACT: 
 The total fiscal impact of Project Prestige for the next thirteen years is estimated to be $3,318,675. Funding for this proposal is available in the OEV budget and will be budgeted as part of the OEV Capital Budget. 
 RECOMMENDED ACTION: 
 Option 1: Approve the Targeted Business Program funding for Project Prestige for a total estimated amount of $2,628,675 over ten years and authorize the Director of PLACE or his designee, to execute an agreement for the commitment of additional funds to Florida A&M University in the amount of $690,000 to be paid over the remaining thirteen (13) years of the Infrastructure Sales Surtax Program. 
 STRATEGIC PLAN: 
 The development of an incentive package for prospective clients directly supports the following Economic Development Strategic Core Strategies: 
 Drive Business Recruitment, Retention, and Expansion 
 Enhance the Incentive Toolbox 
 This incentive package directly supports OEV’s job creation goal to create 100 high-wage jobs in target industry sectors and builds upon the “Magnetic Capital of the World” business development activities. 
 SUPPLEMENTAL INFORMATION: 
 On October 27, 2016, the IA approved the Economic Development Strategic Plan for Tallahassee-Leon County, which reflects the Board’s desire to invest in and cultivate the evolving economic development landscape. During this meeting, the Board also adopted the Policies and Procedures Manual for OEV, which formally guides staff activity, ensures the appropriate and responsible use of organizational resources, and enables OEV to develop a successful, customer-centric approach. These policies, including the local Targeted Business Program (TBP), also benefit the local community by offering competitive economic development incentives. As part of this policy, the Board approved the Intergovernmental Management Committee (IMC) to approve and execute any documents related to local incentive programs of less than $500,000 per program, and any incentive program exceeding $500,000 must be brought to the Board for consideration. 
 Staff is currently working closely with Project Prestige and local and state economic development partners to communicate the benefits of choosing Tallahassee-Leon County over out-of-state competitors for its proposed expansion. To remain competitive, this item requests approval of the itemized incentive package, to encourage the company’s retention and expansion locally. 
 PROJECT OVERVIEW 
 Project Prestige represents a Tallahassee-Leon County-based advanced manufacturing and magnetic technology company considering expansion within Innovation Park. The company practices corporate social responsibility, including setting energy, climate, and environmental sustainability targets, establishing internship opportunities for students enrolled in the FAMU FSU College of Engineering, and making donations to local nonprofits and Leon County Schools. 
 The company's proposed expansion represents a $25 million capital investment, 100 new manufacturing and research jobs over the next 2 years, and a new 50,000 sq. ft. manufacturing center. Based on the project’s known parameters, Project Prestige is eligible to participate in three incentive programs: the Targeted Business Program (TBP), the State Corporate Income Tax Credit Program, and the State of Florida’s Urban Job Tax Credit Program. 
 CONFIDENTIALITY 
 The company did not submit its written request for confidentiality prior to the public meeting of the Competitive Projects Cabinet held on May 21, 2026. The name of the company was therefore disclosed at the public meeting and can be discussed pursuant to the requirements of section 288.075(2), Florida Statutes. 
 Florida law, however, does provide that proprietary confidential business information held by an economic development agency is confidential and exempt from public disclosure until such information is otherwise publicly available or is no longer treated by the company as proprietary confidential business information. 
 ECONOMIC IMPACT ANALYSIS 
 An economic analysis conducted by the FSU Center for Economic Forecasting and Analysis found that Construction and Permanent Employment benefits from the project would equal $106 million in economic output. Of this, $35 million would be a one-time construction impact, and $71.3 million would occur annually once the full number of hires (100) is reached at the average annual salary of $75,000. This will result in 71 indirect and 78 induced jobs created and sustained once the expansion is fully operational and will permanently contribute an additional $71.3 million to the Tallahassee MSA economy thereafter. The forecast estimates that permanent operations will result in $9.4 million in federal and $2.8 million in state and local taxes annually at full buildout (Attachment #1). 
 If approved and the company moves forward, Project Prestige activity is expected to create 100 new full-time jobs over 2 years, with salaries greater than 120% of the local average annual wage, and to invest an estimated $25 million in capital in Leon County. 
 TARGETED BUSINESS PROGRAM (LOCAL) 
 Targeted Business Program (TBP) is a local incentive program designed to foster business growth that benefits the community by advancing the long-term vision for economically viable, environmentally sustainable growth. TBP offers incentives to new and existing businesses that create value-added jobs that will diversify the economy, align with Tallahassee-Leon County’s business mix, and generate revenue growth from the sale of goods and services outside the local economy. While TBP rewards job creation, it is built on a company’s local capital expenditures on land, buildings, and equipment. The greater a company’s outlay for real estate, the greater its potential for TBP reimbursement. If approved, Project Prestige qualifies for 100% reimbursement of permit fees and a portion of ad valorem taxes over ten years. The total estimated TBP incentive for this project is $2,628,675 over the next ten years, which includes an estimated one-time $30,631 reimbursement for development fees in year one, based upon its corporate performance, metric fulfillment, and reimbursement request. It is anticipated that the first reimbursement will be issued in FY 2028. It is anticipated that adequate funding will be available through the allocation of sales tax dollars for economic development. The annual allocation for Project Prestige’s TBP is estimated to range from $382,986 in year one to $198,104 in year ten, with a ten-year average of $262,700. 
 FLORIDA A&M UNIVERSITY SUPPORT FOR PROJECT PRESTIGE SITE DEVELOPMENT 
 Based on discussions with the President of Florida A&M University and her leadership team, the University has expressed its willingness to lease or sublease approximately 7.2 acres of land for the proposed site of Project Prestige at no cost to the company long-term to support the project’s development and operation. The proposed project site, which is leased by Florida A&M University from the State of Florida, specifically the Board of Trustees of the Internal Improvement Trust Fund (“TIITF”), has an estimated appraised value of approximately $690,000. Unlike previous economic development projects involving publicly controlled land assets, Florida A&M University has indicated its support for leveraging the property as part of a broader strategy to advance economic development, innovation, and job creation in Tallahassee-Leon County. As such, the value of the land lease represents a significant local contribution to the successful recruitment and expansion of Project Prestige and further supports the community's long-term economic development objectives. 
 To facilitate the project and support broader economic development opportunities within Innovation Park, OEV recommends that the IA Board provide funding to Florida A&M University commensurate with the appraised value of the proposed project site. In conjunction with this effort, OEV recommends that the parties develop a separate Memorandum of Understanding to support site-readiness activities for the University’s approximately 22.8 remaining acres within Innovation Park. These activities may include due diligence, planning, infrastructure assessments, environmental analysis, and other measures to enhance the site's marketability and development readiness for future commercial and industrial activation opportunities. 
 Additionally, OEV and Florida A&M University have will be entering into a Memorandum of Understanding that authorizes OEV to actively market the University’s Innovation Park properties to prospective businesses and targeted industry sectors. This coordinated approach is intended to strengthen the community’s inventory of development-ready sites, support business recruitment and expansion efforts, and advance the long-term economic competitiveness of Tallahassee-Leon County. 
 OTHER ELIGIBLE STATE INCENTIVE PROGRAMS 
 Project Prestige is also eligible to participate in the State of Florida’s Urban Job Tax Credit Program upon achieving specific job-creation milestones. This funding initiative is tailored for new or existing businesses located in a designated high-crime area by the State of Florida in Tallahassee-Leon County to help encourage quality job growth. It provides eligible businesses that create jobs with a pay-for-performance refund determined by the number of jobs created and the average annual wage of those jobs. It is evaluated and applied annually, and Project Prestige is estimated to be eligible for a total of $100,000 over 10 years. 

 Project Prestige may be eligible for incentives offered through the State of Florida’s Corporate Income Tax Credit Program, which supports qualified business expansion and relocation projects that create high-wage jobs and significant capital investment within targeted industries. The program provides eligible companies with credits against their Florida corporate income tax liabilities based on project-specific criteria, including job creation, average annual wages, capital investment levels, and the project's overall economic impact. Based on preliminary project information, Project Prestige’s proposed capital investment, anticipated job creation, and alignment with Tallahassee-Leon County’s targeted industry sectors may position the company to qualify for consideration under the program. Additionally, the project’s potential to generate new manufacturing activity, expand the local tax base, and create jobs with wages above the regional average further supports its competitiveness for state-level economic development incentives. 

 Any incentive consideration through the State of Florida would require formal review and approval by FloridaCommerce and would remain subject to the company satisfying all applicable statutory requirements, performance metrics, and verification standards established by the State of Florida. 
 COMPETITIVE PROJECTS CABINET: 
 At its May 21, 2026, meeting, the Competitive Projects Cabinet (CPC) unanimously recommended IA Board approval of the incentive package to support Project Prestige, including: 

 Targeted Business Program funding for a total estimated amount of $2,628,675 over ten years; and, 
 Commitment of a market ground rent value to FAMU ($690,000 total over 13-year period) for planning, infrastructure assessments, environmental analysis, and other measures to enhance the site's marketability and development readiness for future commercial and industrial activation opportunities to support its role in future development in Innovation Park within the 22.8 acres of undeveloped land. 
 FUNDING SCHEDULE AND DISTRIBUTION: 
 Should the IA Board approve the local components of the incentive, staff will draft a contract similar to previous incentive awards that ties funding disbursements to proven new employment and wages, and to demonstrable taxes (e.g., ad valorem, tangible personal property, corporate income, and sales tax) paid by the company during eligible timelines. The Targeted Business Program funding represents a total estimated amount of $2,628,675 over ten years. 

 If approved by the IA Board, the PLACE Director will execute the commitment of funds to Florida A&M University in the amount of $690,000 as agreed upon through a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) between FAMU and OEV, to include the following: 
 Funding to support strategic predevelopment activities within the 22.8 acres of undeveloped land 
 The approved funding allocation shall be distributed over the remaining thirteen (13) years of the Infrastructure Sales Surtax Program. Because the project is not anticipated to obtain a Certificate of Occupancy immediately, the initial disbursement made upon issuance of the Certificate of Occupancy shall include the cumulative prorated amount attributable to the period between the execution of the agreement and the date of occupancy. Subsequent disbursements shall be made annually over the remainder of the Surtax Program period . Funding for this proposal is available in the OEV budget and will be budgeted as part of the OEV Capital Budget. It is anticipated that the first FAMU payment will be issued in FY 2028, and the first TBP will be distributed in FY 2029. Therefore, the requested incentives in this package can be covered by the OEV Capital Budget, as shown in Attachment #2. 
 CONCLUSION: 
 Project Prestige consists of an incentive-driven expansion by a major advanced manufacturer in Leon County. If induced, the company is anticipated to invest $25 million in a new 50,000-square-foot advanced manufacturing facility that will create 100 high-wage jobs during the period 2028-2030. 
 The CPC and OEV staff are recommending the IA Board’s approval of Project Prestige’s current $3,318,675 incentive package, including: 
 Targeted Business Program funding for a total estimated amount of $2,628,675 over ten years; and, 
 Commitment of a market ground rent value to FAMU ($690,000 total over 13-year period) for planning, infrastructure assessments, environmental analysis, and other measures to enhance the site's marketability and development readiness for future commercial and industrial activation opportunities to support its role in future development in Innovation Par k within the 22.8 acres of undeveloped land. 

 This investment in asset maximization and predevelopment activities will increase the economic competitiveness of Innovation Park and accommodate the businesses OEV seeks to attract. 
 The approved funding allocation shall be distributed over the remaining thirteen (13) years of the Infrastructure Sales Surtax Program. Because the project is not anticipated to obtain a Certificate of Occupancy immediately, the initial disbursement made upon issuance of the Certificate of Occupancy shall include the cumulative prorated amount attributable to the period between the execution of the agreement and the date of occupancy. Subsequent disbursements shall be made annually over the remainder of the Surtax Program period. The company will make its final decision on expansion in July 2026. Should the IA Board approve the Project Prestige’s incentive packet, staff will continue assisting the company with any planning and permitting needs that arise during the expansion phase. 
 OPTIONS: 
 Option 1: Approve the Targeted Business Program funding for Project Prestige for a total estimated amount of $2,628,675 over ten years and authorize the Director of PLACE or his designee, to execute an agreement for the commitment of additional funds to Florida A&M University in the amount of $690,000 to be paid over the remaining thirteen (13) years of the Infrastructure Sales Surtax Program. 

 Option 2: Do not approve the Project Prestige Incentive Package. 
 Option 3: IA Board Direction. 

 RECOMMENDED ACTION: 
 Option 1: Approve the Targeted Business Program funding for Project Prestige for a total estimated amount of $2,628,675 over ten years and authorize the Director of PLACE or his designee, to execute an agreement for the commitment of additional funds to Florida A&M University in the amount of $690,000 to be paid over the remaining thirteen (13) years of the Infrastructure Sales Surtax Program.

 Project Prestige Economic Impact Results

 Recommended Action

Morgan and Sons, Inc. for Southeast Farm Operation and Management Services, at a fixed annual price of $195,000 for an initial term of five years commencing October 17, 2026, with an option to renew for an additional five years. 

 For more information, please contact: Rob McGarrah, General Manager, Underground Utilities & Public Infrastructure, (850) 891-5109, or Andrew Platt, Underground Utilities & Public Infrastructure, (850) 891-6148 

 Statement of Issue 
 This agenda item seeks City Commission approval of an amendment to the existing contract with J.L. Morgan & Sons, Inc. for operation and management services at the Southeast Farm (SEF), establishing an initial five-year term with an option to renew for an additional five years if an evaluation of the farming operation and regulatory requirements determines the renewal is in the City's best interest. The SEF is a critical component of the City's wastewater treatment system and requires specialized agricultural management to comply with Florida Department of Environmental Protection permit requirements. Morgan has successfully managed the SEF under these unique operational and regulatory conditions for more than 28 years and remains the only qualified provider identified through the City's procurement and market outreach efforts. 

 Recommended Action 
 Option 1: Authorize the City Manager, or designee, to negotiate and execute an amendment to Contract No. 5161 with J.L. Morgan and Sons, Inc. for Southeast Farm Operation and Management Services, at a fixed annual price of $195,000 for an initial term of five years commencing October 17, 2026, with an option to renew for an additional five years. 

 Fiscal Impact 
 Total funding required for the initial five-year term and optional five-year extension is $1,950,000, payable in quarterly installments over the ten-year period. The annual cost remains unchanged from the City's current agreement with J.L. Morgan & Sons, Inc. 

 Supplemental Material/Issue Analysis 

 History/Facts & Issues 
 The City of Tallahassee beneficially reuses reclaimed water from the Thomas P. Smith Water Reclamation Facility (TPS) through agricultural irrigation at the 3,860-acre Southeast Farm (SEF), a Florida Department of Environmental Protection (FDEP)-permitted slow-rate land application system. The majority of reclaimed water is applied through center-pivot irrigation systems to non-edible crops and vegetative cover, supporting the beneficial reuse of reclaimed water while minimizing impacts to natural resources. 

 The FDEP operating permit requires the SEF to maximize nitrogen removal through crop production while prohibiting the use of supplemental fertilizer. These permit requirements create unique agricultural and operational challenges that require specialized expertise in crop selection, rotation, harvesting, and farm management under low-nutrient reclaimed water irrigation conditions. 

 Agricultural operations at the SEF began in the early 1980s under a lease arrangement with private farming operators. J. L. Morgan & Sons, Inc. (Morgan) was awarded the lease in 1997. Following a 2005 settlement agreement related to the protection of Wakulla Springs, the City's permit requirements became more restrictive, including lower nutrient concentrations in reclaimed water and prohibitions on fertilizer use and livestock grazing. As a result, the City transitioned from a lease arrangement to a professional services contract for specialized farm management. Morgan was awarded the initial contract in 2008 and, due to its demonstrated expertise operating the SEF under these unique conditions, the contract was extended in 2013. 

 In 2016, the City competitively solicited Southeast Farm operation and management services and conducted outreach to encourage participation from qualified firms. Despite these efforts, Morgan was the only respondent, and the City entered into a new five-year contract. In 2021, after additional market outreach identified no other qualified providers capable of meeting the SEF's specialized operational and regulatory requirements, the City entered into a new five-year sole-source contract with Morgan (Contract No. 5161). 

 This agenda item proposes amending the current agreement to establish an initial five-year term commencing October 17, 2026, with an option for one additional five-year renewal term. Prior to the expiration of the initial five-year term, the City will evaluate the farming operation and regulatory requirements to determine whether renewal is in the City's best interest. If the City elects to exercise the renewal option, the agreement will continue for an additional five-year term, unless otherwise modified or terminated in accordance with the Agreement. If the renewal term is exercised, the City will conduct a market analysis prior to its expiration to evaluate the availability of qualified providers and determine the appropriate next contracting course of action. 

 Department(s) Review 
 Procurement Services 

 Options 
 1. Authorize the City Manager, or designee, to negotiate and execute an amendment to Contract No. 5161 with J.L. Morgan and Sons, Inc. for Southeast Farm Operation and Management Services, at a fixed annual price of $195,000 for an initial term of five years commencing October 17, 2026, with an option to renew for an additional five years. 

 2. Provide staff with alternate direction. 

 Attachments/References 
 None
